glosses: A skirmish, a hostile encounter.

examples.text:
In Anatolia tensions between state officials (ehl-i örf) and the peasants were strained to breaking point.
At several places—particularly in the frontier provinces—there were fierce clashes between the janissaries stationed there and the governors. In Aleppo and Damascus incidents were common after 1589: the kuls threw rocks at the beylerbeyi’s house, killed people, broke into the divan several times and took the money prepared by the council for remittance to the centre.

glosses: A combination of garments that do not look good together, especially because of conflicting colours.

examples.text: She was wearing a horrible clash of red and orange.

glosses: To make a clashing sound.

examples.text: The cymbals clashed.

glosses: To cause to make a clashing sound.

examples.text: Thorfinn clashed his shield against Vallon's and swung his axe to hook Vallon's ankle.

glosses: To come into violent conflict.

examples.text: Fans from opposing teams clashed on the streets after the game.

glosses: To argue angrily.

examples.text: My parents often clashed about minor things, such as the cleaning or shopping rota.

glosses: To face each other in an important game.

examples.text: The veteran American legend claims he and Welsh two-weight world champion Calzaghe will clash on 20 September, probably at The MGM Grand in Las Vegas.

glosses: To fail to look good together; to contrast unattractively; to fail to harmonize.

examples.text: You can't wear that shirt! It clashes with your trousers.
The hotel room was ugly, and the wallpaper clashed with the carpet.

glosses: To coincide, to happen at the same time, thereby rendering it impossible to attend all.

examples.text: I can't come to your wedding because it clashes with a friend's funeral.
I wanted to take German, but it clashed with art on the timetable.

glosses: To chatter or gossip.
To play Clash Royale or Clash of Clans.

examples.text: Dude, are we clashing tonight?
